correctness.rationale: Every prefix of an overlap-free word is overlap-free. For each one-bit extension, a factor of length 2p+1 has period p exactly when it is axaxa with |x|=p-1; this includes p=1. The supplied recurrence removes the final nonempty square, so correctly computes maximum square count; for this theorem the exact-nine test can also be done independently without relying on the distinction between at least nine and exactly nine. The independent reproduction checked every possible start of a forbidden factor and counted factorizations at each exact depth, with the empty prefix having depth zero and only positive-length even square edges allowed. It found zero exactly-nine words at each length 1–47, then 416 overlap-free words at length 48 of which exactly the displayed complementary pair admit nine squares. Each has exactly one ordered cut, with lengths (6,4,4,4,12,4,4,4,6). Replay: python /workspace/branches/0ba74666-1385-4be6-8d72-124807c92212/independent_census.py; its output is independent_census.log in the same directory. This is a finite exact exhaustion, not a statement about longer words or other alphabets.
